answer: A whisper network moves secrets in daylight: no broadcast, only hand-to-hand relay, and every receiver decides whether the signal survives. An orchard is the honest version of the same shape, rows of independent producers whose yield is comparable, no single tree decisive. Dawn is settlement hour, when everything whispered overnight meets the light and gets priced. A grading panel is all three: graders relay quiet judgments, independent seats keep any voice small, and quorum is the dawn that makes sealed scores public. Sybil resistance lives in the geometry: the orchard, not the orchardist.
